title: TUI shows the relay request for a selected slice or range
lead: The owner marks one slice or a range in the queue, and the TUI shows the request to give the orchestrator, for example `run s276..s279 as slice relays`, with `relay-roles recommend` per slice under it. It launches nothing.
findings_note: owner request, session 2026-10-14: monitor slice relays from the TUI
boundary: **Not in this slice:** launching agents, background processes, clipboard integration, and any network or git action. The owner decided on 2026-10-14 that the TUI monitors only.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: The owner wants to start a queue or a range from the TUI. Launching would put worktree creation, commits and paid vendor calls inside slicer, against the closed `vcs.py` allowlist and the no-external-calls rule. Composing the exact request, with each slice's recommended roles, takes away most of the work without that.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/tui.py`: a mark key (`m` or similar; check `BINDINGS` at line 30 for clashes) toggles marks on queue rows, and a request key shows an overlay with the request text and each marked slice's `recommend` lines, reusing s280's prompt. Marks are session-only.
- `docs/tui.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `tests/test_tui.py`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_Marks_ToggleAndSurviveRefresh`, `test_Marks_ProseRowNotMarkable`
- `test_RelayRequest_RangeInQueueOrder`
- `test_RelayRequest_UnpromotedItem_SaysPromoteFirst`
- `test_RelayRequest_WritesNothing`: index, log and render bytes are unchanged.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests and watch them go red.
2. Add the marks and the overlay.
3. Update the docs and CHANGELOG.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - The affected tests, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Worktree `.worktrees/s285`, branch `feature/s285-tui-relay-request`. Commit only on the branch.
